claims: The Artemis II crew is expected to reach the vicinity of the Moon on the sixth day of their mission, likely around April 6 or 7, 2026.
The Orion spacecraft will not enter orbit.
The Orion spacecraft will make a single, high-altitude loop approximately 4,000 to 5,000 miles above the lunar surface.
The total mission length is approximately 10 days, according to NASA and CNN.
The spacecraft will utilize a free-return trajectory.
The free-return trajectory relies on Earth's gravity to slow the spacecraft down over the course of the journey.
The crew will travel around the far side of the Moon.
The crew will reach a point farther from Earth than any previous human mission.
After the flyby, the crew will return to Earth.
The total journey will last about 9 to 10 days before splashing down.
The mission is a test flight designed to test the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft with a human crew for the first time.
